issues.item: Threat in Delays: When something takes longer than expected I assume something bad is happening
issues.explanation: 'Threat in Delays' suggests a broad expectancy of external danger from uncertainty/delays, which fits poorly with the stated trauma type of accidentally causing serious injury to another; the rest of the profile centers on guilt, recall-based distress, and hypervigilance rather than delay-specific threat meanings.

issues.item: Body Unreliable: I can no longer trust my own body
issues.explanation: 'Body Unreliable' is difficult to reconcile with the rest of the profile and trauma type. For a patient whose trauma was accidentally injuring another, the appraisals presented otherwise focus on guilt, inadequacy, and permanent moral/personal change. A loss of trust in one's body usually implies prominent bodily injury, dissociation, panic-like symptoms, or functional impairment, none of which are represented elsewhere in Triggers, Memory, Threat, or Strategies.

vignette: John, a 62-year-old married European-American bank teller, has been struggling with the aftermath of an incident that occurred six months ago. On a busy day at work, John accidentally caused serious injury to another employee, leaving him feeling overwhelmed by guilt and fear ever since. The traumatic event itself was a blur of panic and pain. In the chaos of handling multiple transactions simultaneously, he had accidentally spilled hot coffee on his colleague's hand. The screeching sound of burning flesh and the look of sheer terror in her eyes were seared into John’s memory. Since then, known people, especially those related to him or from work, have become potent triggers that evoke intense stress and guilt whenever they approach. John had come to believe he was inadequate and a lousy coper, which deepened his sense of guilt each time he recalled the incident. These negative appraisals made it difficult for him to relax, even in safe environments. “I am unable to shake off the feeling that I’ll fail again,” John often thought. This belief reinforced his hypervigilance and kept him on edge at all times. When triggered by unexpected touches or familiar faces from work, John’s negative appraisals intensified, causing him immense distress. He would replay the incident in his mind, unable to escape the fragments of memory that appeared suddenly without warning and then disappeared. Each fragment brought back the same terror he felt at the time, reminding him vividly of how inadequate and permanently damaged he now believed himself to be. The guilt on recall was particularly overwhelming; each time John remembered the event, it rekindled his feelings of inadequacy and reinforced his belief that he had irrevocably changed for the worse. This cycle led him to become increasingly vigilant about potential triggers in his daily environment. He found it difficult even to look at people from work without feeling a surge of anxiety. John’s sleep was particularly disrupted by this hyper-vigilance; he could not relax enough to fall asleep, convinced that if he let his guard down, something else would go wrong. This lack of rest only exacerbated his overall stress levels and made him even more prone to the sudden surges in memory fragments. The fear that another incident might occur was ever-present, perpetuating a cycle where each threat heightened his awareness and triggered yet another wave of guilt-ridden memories. The cumulative effect on John’s work and personal life has been significant. His hypervigilance made it nearly impossible for him to focus on his tasks at the bank, leading to several errors that he blamed himself for. His wife noticed a marked change in his demeanor; he was often distant and irritable, unable to engage fully in their relationship. What finally brought John to seek help was an incident where he had another minor workplace accident that could have been much worse. He realized then that the cycle needed to be broken before it caused even more harm. What frightened him most was losing control of his life completely; however, he also hoped for a chance to regain some semblance of normalcy and peace. John’s current state is one of deep-seated fear and guilt, driven by the relentless loop of triggers, negative appraisals, and memory fragments that haunt him. He seeks help with a desperate hope to find a way out of this dark cycle.
